walkthrough:
In right-angled triangle $\triangle BPC$ (with $BC = 3$ and hypotenuse $BP = AB = 5$):
$$\cos(\angle PBC) = \frac{BC}{BP} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6 \implies \angle PBC = \cos^{-1}(0.6) \approx 0.927295\text{ radians}$$

Because $\angle ABC = \frac{\pi}{2}$ radians in rectangle $ABCD$:
$$\angle ABP = \frac{\pi}{2} - \angle PBC = \frac{\pi}{2} - 0.927295 = 0.643501 \approx 0.6435\text{ radians} \quad (\text{to 4 d.p.})$$

ai_rubric.Angle Proof: Calculates $\angle PBC = 0.9273\text{ rad}$ and subtracts from $\pi/2$ to show $\angle ABP = 0.6435\text{ rad}$ (M1).

walkthrough:
Calculate the area of circular sector $BAP$ (radius $5$, angle $0.643501\text{ rad}$):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } BAP) = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(5^2)(0.643501) = 12.5 \times 0.643501 \approx 8.0438 \approx 8.04\text{ units}^2$$

Calculate the area of circular sector $DAQ$ (radius $3$, central angle $\angle ADQ = \frac{\pi}{2}$ radians):
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } DAQ) = \frac{1}{2}(3^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \frac{9\pi}{4} \approx 7.0686 \approx 7.07\text{ units}^2$$

ai_rubric.Sector Areas: Applies $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ (M1). Obtains area of $BAP = 8.04$ (A1) and area of $DAQ = 7.07$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding Areas of Composite Circular Regions

hints: Rectangle area is $15$, triangle $BPC$ area is $\frac{1}{2}(3)(4) = 6$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of rectangle $ABCD$ and right triangle $\triangle BPC$ ($PC = \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4$):
$$\text{Area}(ABCD) = 5 \times 3 = 15$$
$$\text{Area}(\triangle BPC) = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 = 6$$

Calculate the area of the region outside both sectors by inclusion-exclusion:
$$\text{Area}(ABCD) - \text{Area}(\triangle BPC) = 15 - 6 = 9$$

Calculate the shaded overlap area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}(\text{sector } BAP) + \text{Area}(\text{sector } DAQ) - 9$$
$$= 8.0438 + 7.0686 - 9 = 15.1124 - 9 = 6.1124 \approx 6.11\text{ units}^2 \quad (\text{to 3 s.f.})$$

ai_rubric.Shaded Area Strategy: Applies sector sum minus unshaded region (M1). Finds triangle area $6$ (A1). Obtains shaded area $6.11\text{ units}^2$ (A1).
